c.tagline: A Tibetan-plateau town of golden monasteries, grasslands and the gateway to the eastern Himalaya.

taxi.fareNote: Didi is the easiest way to book a car; metered street taxis are cheap but drivers often prefer a flat rate to the monastery, Napahai or the airport. The Dukezong Old Town lanes are pedestrian, so cars drop you at the gates.

emergency.note: 110 is police, 120 the ambulance and 119 fire. At 3,200 m altitude take it easy on arrival - clinics stock oxygen for altitude sickness. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or written Chinese address helps.

avoid.reason: Altitude sickness is the main risk on arrival; be wary of hard-sell 'Tibetan medicine' and gallery stops on tours.

hood_desc: The 1,300-year-old Tibetan old town on Guishan Hill, a warren of cobbled lanes, timber Tibetan houses, cafes and guesthouses crowned by the giant golden prayer wheel; atmospheric and walkable, the most characterful base despite a 2014 fire and its careful rebuild.

Modern Shangri-La spreading below the old town, with the bus station, hospitals, supermarkets, chain hotels and everyday services; the practical, convenient base for transport and for acclimatising to the altitude before heading out.

The area about five kilometres north around Ganden Sumtseling, Yunnan's largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery (a 'little Potala'), overlooking the mirror-like Lamu Yangcuo lake; a serene, sights-focused base among monasteries and meadows.

The seasonal grassland lake about eight kilometres northwest, a Ramsar wetland and black-necked-crane haven ringed by pastures and Tibetan villages; a scenic, quiet base for wide-open highland landscapes and horseback rides.

A pastoral valley about twenty kilometres south along the G214 toward Lijiang, famed for autumn colours, barley fields and 'ten-thousand-flower' meadows; a tranquil rural base close to Napa and the road out.
lodging: Arro Khampa by Zinc Journey Shangri-La

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; the 3,200 m altitude makes hydration important.

transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as cash and cards are increasingly awkward. Taxis and Didi are paid the same way.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 7am-8pm; after that use Didi or a taxi. Many outlying sights are best reached by chartered car.
transit.note: Shangri-La has no metro or rail transit; getting around means a handful of city bus lines, Didi and taxis, plus walking the pedestrian old town. Sights are spread across the plateau, so most visitors charter a car or join a tour for Songzanlin, Napahai and Pudacuo.

train: Lijiang-Shangri-La railway (opened November 2023) with trains to Lijiang, Dali and Kunming
bus: Intercity coaches to Lijiang, Dali, Kunming and Deqin (Meili Snow Mountain)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to downtown Shangri-La (~20 min)
Taxi or Didi to the old town (~15 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels; a small tip for a private trekking guide or driver is at your discretion.
